newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED FIRMER ON MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED FIRMER ON MONDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted firmer on Monday, largely in reaction to a rise in annual inflation in March, dealers said.
"Rates are now being quoted higher. It seems the market is at last reacting to the rise in inflation to 19.9 percent in March," one dealer said.
He said there had been increasing concern in the market of late over the margin between inflation and money rates, seen too wide at around three percentage points.

On Monday, the central Reserve Bank auctioned Z$175 million worth of treasury bills at 16.49 percent, up from 16.02 percent and discount houses were selling the central bank paper in the secondary market at 16.25 percent.

NCDs with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 17 percent from 16.75 and sold at 16.85 percent from 16.35 percent. Bank bills edged up to 16.50 and 16.25 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 16.25 and 16 percent while call money firmed to 16 percent from 15.75 percent.
Reserve Bank figures indicated an opening market shortage of Z$247 million from a previous deficit of Z$32.5 million.
